candidate.title: TRAP-Seq
candidate.scope: The single TRAP-Seq row of the supplied Illumina poster, labeled “Targeted purification of polysomal mRNA (TRAP-Seq)”: capped polysomal RNA, antibody-mediated capture on a bead, RNA isolation, and reverse transcription to terminal cDNA. The matching catalogue page confirms this schematic scope. The poster-cited Jiao and Meyerowitz plant study clarifies the tag–ribosome affinity interface and readout limitations; its complete experimental preparation is not asserted by this schematic. The left RNA/ribosome thumbnail is an overview icon. The separately labeled HiTS-RAP and DLAF rows and the right-hand chemical legend are surrounding context; this row has one route and no depicted alternative or split. Downstream sequencing is described in text; no adapter construction or sequencing operation is drawn.

features: Purple RNA bearing a black square labeled Cap and multiple blue ribosome icons; the left overview thumbnail also labels RNA.
The accompanying method description specifies tagged ribosomal proteins expressed in cells. In the cited plant implementation, tagged L18 is incorporated into polysomes.

operations.label: Polysomes → Bead
operations.description: Affinity-capture the input RNA–ribosome complexes on the depicted bead. The resulting material retains the RNA with its ribosomes and adds attachment through the antibody-shaped connectors to the support.
operations.mechanism: Antibody recognition of an epitope-tagged ribosomal protein captures the associated RNA–ribosome complex. The drawing leaves the tag unspecified. In the poster-cited Jiao and Meyerowitz implementation, the protein is His/FLAG-tagged L18 (HF–RPL18), and anti-FLAG M2 affinity gel provides capture.
operations.information_effect: Enriches the RNA pool associated with the targeted ribosomes. When tag expression is restricted to a cell domain, the captured fraction acquires that domain association. Co-precipitation is evidence of ribosome association and does not by itself prove productive translation of every recovered RNA.

operations.description: Isolate the RNA associated with the captured polysome fraction. The output is RNA available for reverse transcription, with the bead and ribosome complex removed from the depicted material carrier.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Use the recovered RNA as template to synthesize cDNA. The RNA-to-blue-strand change labeled Reverse transcription leads to the terminal blue product labeled cDNA; no additional transformation is named on the final arrow.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription copies the selected RNA sequence information into DNA; no particular primer, reverse transcriptase, or internal library-preparation sequence is specified by this row.
operations.information_effect: The cDNA carries a sequence representation of the captured RNA pool for deep sequencing. The supported readout identifies and quantifies ribosome-associated transcripts and can reveal transcript structures, including splice isoforms. Cell-domain attribution derives from restricted tag expression in the cited implementation; ribosome association remains the basis for calling the RNAs “translating”.

method_scopes.rationale: All three operations belong to the single TRAP-Seq target named by the card and the row. The matched collection page has the same target heading and describes tag-based ribosome purification, associated RNA isolation and cDNA synthesis. The primary paper explicitly calls the combination of TRAP and RNA-seq “TRAP-seq”; embedded TRAP is the affinity-purification component, not an additional target workflow. The figure is a schematic of this architecture, with the cited plant implementation clarifying the affinity interface. Its generic tag symbols do not establish identical complete protocols for all TRAP implementations. The multiple ribosome icons depict polysomes without specifying a measured ribosome count or count-selection threshold. The initial thumbnail is descriptive and is not connected as an extra preparation branch.
